tapeLine: Thursday 22 October was a tech-led sell-off: Nasdaq about -2.6% to roughly 26,008, S&P 500 about -1.2% to roughly 7,663, Dow roughly flat near 52,868, per Korea Times (23 Oct) and Reuters-sourced recaps. Friday futures levels were not found.
matters:
The Nasdaq had its worst day since June as AI-spending worries returned: the Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 6.7%, its largest daily drop since 23 June, per Korea Times (23 Oct).

Meta fell about 7% despite beating estimates, after reporting its first cash outflow in more than a decade on AI spending; Tesla fell 3.1% after positive free cash flow and a cut to 2026 capex plans, per Korea Times (23 Oct).

Rising oil prices were cited as an added source of unease ahead of next week’s Fed meeting, per the same report; no oil level was found with a dated source.

Invalidation: the S&P 500 closed about 2% below its 7,811.54 record close of 9 October; whether it holds below Tuesday’s 7,712.57 close or reclaims it is the open question.
alsoOnTape: Oil, gold, Treasury yield and VIX levels for Wednesday were not found with a dated source and are not carried.

regime.tag: The tentative stabilisation of recent sessions broke on Thursday: the Nasdaq fell about 2.6% and the semiconductor index 6.7% on renewed AI-spending doubts, while the Dow held flat.
regime.sizing: No scheduled macro catalyst was confirmed for Friday; the 27-28 October FOMC is the next scheduled event.

secondOrder: Leadership reversed within a day: Wednesday’s AI-led rally was undone by Thursday’s AI-cost sell-off, while the Dow, less exposed to semiconductors, finished flat. That is an observation, not a forecast.

scorecard.text: The prior regime call, tentative stabilisation, did not survive Thursday: the S&P 500 fell about 1.2% to roughly 7,663, below Wednesday’s 7,757.17, per Korea Times (23 Oct).
The prior Nasdaq floor failed: Monday’s 26,430.89 was broken, with the Nasdaq closing near 26,008.
The prior secondOrder framing of leadership returning to AI and tech reversed within a day as semiconductors fell 6.7%.
The prior note that Meta and Tesla results were the open evidence was borne out: Meta fell about 7% and Tesla 3.1%, per Korea Times (23 Oct).
Whether yields kept falling after the PPI print still cannot be graded: no sourced yield levels were found.
The 27-28 October FOMC has not occurred.
